title: ExPOSE: a Revealing Look at Plant Cells Through Expansion Microscopy
content: Expansion Microscopy (ExM) reimagines the traditional fluorescence microscopy approach for high-resolution visualization of labeled molecules in biological systems: instead of being constrained by conventional diffraction-limited optics in light microscopy, researchers can linearly enlarge cells and tissues and their contents to enhance resolution, even with conventional optical imaging systems [1]. To achieve physical expansion, fixed cells or tissues are covalently bound to a swellable hydrogel mesh, which can be expanded using deionized water. ExM is a versatile tool and enables isotropic linear expansion of various specimen components, including proteins, nucleic acids, and lipid membranes [2]. Expansion increases the physical distances between biological components, effectively enabling higher resolution by the expansion factor (EF) of the sample. This robust approach resolves fluorescently labeled structures at the sub-organelle level.
